title: CSI Division 03 Concrete
content: Concrete placement, curing, and formwork sequencing for commercial work. Verify mix design, cold-weather protections, and strength tests before stripping forms. Break cylinders at 7 and 28 days; do not strip vertical forms before initial set or slabs before 500-750 psi per ACI 347 guidance.

title: CSI Division 04 Masonry
content: CMU and brick veneer coordination: mortar joint tooling, control joint spacing (typically 20-25 ft or per manufacturer), weep holes at 24-32 in on center, and flashing above openings to shed water out of the cavity.

title: CSI Division 05 Metals / Structural Steel
content: Structural steel erection sequencing: verify anchor bolt survey before steel delivery, torque bolts per RCSC specification (snug-tight then turn-of-nut or DTI washers for slip-critical), and confirm AISC-certified fabricator shop drawings before fabrication release.

title: CSI Division 06 Wood, Plastics, Composites / Rough Framing
content: Rough framing sequence: sill plate with sill sealer and anchor bolts at 6 ft o.c. max, floor joists per span tables, wall studs at 16 in o.c. (24 in for advanced framing), and roof truss bracing per manufacturer's truss placement diagram before sheathing.

title: CSI Division 07 Thermal and Moisture Protection
content: Building envelope continuity: weather-resistive barrier lapped shingle-style over flashing, self-adhered membrane at penetrations and rough openings, and continuous insulation to reduce thermal bridging per IECC climate zone requirements.

title: CSI Division 07 Roofing Systems
content: Low-slope roofing (TPO/EPDM) requires tapered insulation for positive drainage, hot-air or adhesive-welded seams inspected by a probe test, and perimeter/corner enhanced fastening per wind uplift design. Steep-slope shingle roofs need ice-and-water shield at eaves/valleys and proper nailing pattern per manufacturer wind rating.

title: CSI Division 08 Openings / Windows and Doors
content: Window and door rough opening tolerances: typically 1/2 in larger than unit width/height for shim space, flashing integrated with WRB using a sill pan and head flashing, and fire-rated door assemblies must retain listed hardware and self-closing devices.

title: CSI Division 09 Finishes
content: Drywall, flooring, and paint coordination with punch and closeout. Tape and finish to Level 4 or 5 per specification before priming; protect finished floors and casework during remaining trades and MEP commissioning.

title: CSI Division 09 Painting and Coatings
content: Sequence painting after drywall finishing, HVAC balancing dust settles, and prior to flooring installation. Verify moisture content of substrates and manufacturer-required recoat windows; document VOC compliance for occupied buildings.

title: CSI Division 21 Fire Suppression
content: Sprinkler system coordination: hydraulic calculations sized to hazard classification (light/ordinary/extra), head spacing per NFPA 13, and fire pump/backflow testing before certificate of occupancy.

title: CSI Division 22 Plumbing Rough-In
content: Plumbing rough-in sequencing: DWV slope minimum 1/4 in per foot, vent stack sizing per fixture unit count, and pressure test supply lines before insulation/drywall cover. Coordinate sleeve locations with structural before concrete placement.

title: CSI Division 23 HVAC
content: HVAC ductwork sizing follows Manual D/ACCA calculations; seal all joints per SMACNA leakage class, balance air per Manual J load, and commission economizer/BAS controls before TAB report sign-off.

title: CSI Division 26 Electrical Fundamentals
content: Electrical rough-in: panel schedule load calculations per NEC Article 220, conduit fill limited to 40% for 3+ conductors, and GFCI/AFCI protection required per NEC 210.8/210.12 in wet and habitable locations respectively.

title: CTE Electrical Fundamentals
content: Ohm's law (V=IR), conduit fill awareness, and lockout/tagout fundamentals for CTE electrical pathways. Series circuits share current, parallel circuits share voltage; always verify de-energized state with a rated meter before touching conductors.

title: AIA A201 General Conditions
content: Contractual roles for owner, architect, and contractor. Change orders require written authorization and time/price impact documentation. The architect interprets contract documents; disputes route through the initial decision maker before mediation/arbitration per Article 15.

title: AIA A101 Owner-Contractor Agreement Basics
content: Stipulated-sum agreements fix the contract sum subject to authorized change orders; cost-plus agreements reimburse cost plus fee with a guaranteed maximum price (GMP) commonly used to share savings/overruns per negotiated terms.

title: OSHA Fall Protection
content: Fall protection triggers at 6 ft in construction (29 CFR 1926.501). Inspect harnesses and anchor points daily; guardrails, safety nets, or personal fall arrest systems are the three accepted control methods. A competent person must evaluate the work area continuously.

title: OSHA Trenching and Excavation Safety
content: Trenches 5 ft or deeper require protective systems (sloping, shoring, or shielding) unless in stable rock, per 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P. A competent person must classify soil type (A, B, or C) and inspect daily and after rain events.

title: OSHA Scaffold Safety
content: Scaffolds must be erected, moved, and dismantled under the supervision of a competent person, capable of supporting 4x the intended load, with guardrails above 10 ft and full planking with no more than 1 in gaps.

title: OSHA Crane and Rigging Safety
content: Only qualified/certified operators may run cranes per 1926 Subpart CC; establish a controlled lift plan for critical picks, verify load charts against radius/boom angle, and maintain a minimum approach distance from energized power lines.

title: Bid Leveling Checklist
content: Normalize alternates, allowances, unit prices, exclusions, and schedule assumptions before award recommendation. Confirm bonding capacity, insurance certificates, and scope clarifications are captured in a written qualification log for every subcontractor bid.

title: Quantity Takeoff Estimating Method
content: Takeoff quantities from drawings by CSI division, apply unit costs from historical data or RSMeans, add waste factors (5-15% depending on trade), and separate labor, material, equipment, and subcontractor cost buckets before applying markup and contingency.

title: RFI Best Practices
content: Write RFIs with drawing references, conflict description, schedule impact, and a proposed solution for faster architect response. Log RFI issue and response dates to prove schedule impact if a delay claim becomes necessary.

title: Submittal Review Workflow
content: Submittals route subcontractor > general contractor (GC review/stamp) > architect/engineer for approval; track long-lead items (switchgear, elevators, curtain wall) separately and start submittal review before mobilization to protect the schedule.

title: Pay Application SOV
content: Align schedule of values to cost codes for AIA-style G702/G703 billing. Retainage (commonly 5-10%) and stored materials must match contract terms; never bill above actual percent complete to avoid over-billing exposure.

title: Job Cost Variance
content: Compare committed cost, actual cost, and forecast (estimate to complete) weekly by cost code. Flag overruns before pay apps are certified and update the job cost forecast so surprises never surface only at project closeout.

title: Change Order Pricing and Documentation
content: Price change orders with labor, material, equipment, sub markup, and overhead/profit consistent with the contract's markup schedule; document time impact with a fragnet showing the change tied into the critical path schedule.

title: Critical Path Method Scheduling
content: CPM scheduling identifies the longest sequence of dependent activities (the critical path) with zero float; activities off the critical path have float that can absorb minor delays without moving substantial completion.

title: Schedule Delay and Time Impact Analysis
content: A time impact analysis inserts a delay fragnet into the as-planned schedule to isolate its net effect on the critical path, distinguishing excusable/compensable delays (owner-caused) from non-excusable delays (contractor-caused).

title: Punch List and Substantial Completion
content: Substantial completion means the owner can use the space for its intended purpose; a punch list documents remaining minor items with responsible party and target date, typically completed within a defined retainage-release window.

title: Warranty Closeout Package
content: Collect O&M manuals, attic stock, training attendance, and warranty start dates before substantial completion. A complete closeout binder protects the owner and reduces post-occupancy callback disputes.

title: Quality Control Inspection Hold Points
content: Establish inspection hold points before concealment (rebar before pour, rough-in before drywall, waterproofing before backfill) with photo documentation logged by date, location, and inspector to defend against future defect claims.

title: Building Code Basics (IBC)
content: The International Building Code classifies occupancy (A, B, E, F, H, I, M, R, S, U) and construction type (I-V, fire-resistance rated) which together set allowable height/area, egress width, and fire separation requirements.

title: Means of Egress Requirements
content: Egress capacity is calculated from occupant load using code-prescribed factors per square foot by use; two remote exits are typically required above defined occupant thresholds, with maximum common path of travel and dead-end corridor limits per IBC Chapter 10.

title: ADA Accessibility Basics
content: ADA/ANSI A117.1 requires accessible routes with 36 in min clear width, ramps at 1:12 max slope, accessible restroom clearances, and door hardware operable with a closed fist (lever, not knob) without tight grasping.

title: Sitework and Erosion Control
content: SWPPP (Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan) requires silt fence/inlet protection before land disturbance, stabilized construction entrance to limit tracking, and inspection after every 0.5 in rain event per NPDES permit conditions.

title: Earthwork and Compaction Testing
content: Compact structural fill in lifts (typically 8-12 in loose) and verify with a nuclear density gauge or sand-cone test to reach the specified percent of Standard/Modified Proctor before placing footings or slabs.

title: Concrete Slab-on-Grade Best Practices
content: Provide a vapor retarder directly under slabs per ACI 302, control joints at roughly 24-36x slab thickness (in feet) spacing, and avoid finishing (troweling) before bleed water evaporates to prevent surface crazing.

title: Curtain Wall and Building Envelope Testing
content: Perform mock-up water penetration testing (ASTM E1105) and air infiltration testing (ASTM E783) on curtain wall systems before full production run to catch flashing/sealant failures early.

title: LEED and Sustainable Construction
content: LEED certification tracks credits across sustainable sites, water efficiency, energy/atmosphere, materials/resources, and indoor environmental quality; construction waste management plans (diverting 50-75%+ from landfill) are a common low-cost credit.

title: Prefabrication and Modular Construction
content: Prefabricated MEP racks and modular volumetric units compress field schedule by shifting labor to a controlled factory environment; success depends on early tolerance coordination (design for manufacture and assembly) between trades.

title: Insurance and Bonding Basics
content: Performance and payment bonds guarantee project completion and subcontractor/supplier payment; commercial general liability and builder's risk insurance protect against third-party claims and property loss during construction, respectively.

title: Lien Rights and Notice Requirements
content: Mechanic's lien rights protect unpaid contractors/suppliers but require strict statutory notices (preliminary notice, notice of intent) and filing deadlines that vary by state; missing a deadline can forfeit lien rights entirely.

title: Confined Space Entry Safety
content: Permit-required confined spaces (manholes, tanks, vaults) need atmospheric testing for oxygen/toxics/flammability, continuous ventilation, an attendant outside, and a rescue plan before any entry per 29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA.

title: Silica Dust and Respiratory Protection
content: OSHA's respirable crystalline silica standard (1926.1153) requires engineering controls (wet cutting, vacuum dust collection) for concrete cutting/grinding tasks, with a written exposure control plan and medical surveillance above action levels.

title: CSI Division 10 Specialties
content: Division 10 covers toilet partitions, lockers, fire extinguishers, signage, and access flooring. Coordinate rough-in blocking for wall-mounted accessories before drywall, verify ADA reach ranges for dispensers, and sequence fire extinguisher cabinets after paint but before final inspection.

title: CSI Division 11 Equipment
content: Kitchen, lab, and industrial equipment require early submittal review for utility rough-ins (gas, water, electrical, exhaust). Verify floor loading, seismic anchorage, and manufacturer startup/commissioning requirements before substantial completion.

title: CSI Division 12 Furnishings
content: Loose furnishings and window treatments are often owner-furnished/contractor-installed (OFCI). Protect finished surfaces during delivery, verify anchor ratings for wall-mounted casework, and coordinate installation after final clean but before owner move-in.

title: CSI Division 13 Special Construction
content: Pre-engineered metal buildings, clean rooms, and modular units need foundation/settlement tolerances verified before erection. Anchor bolt templates must match shop drawings; field welding requires qualified welders and inspection per AWS D1.1 when applicable.

title: CSI Division 14 Conveying Equipment
content: Elevators and escalators are long-lead items requiring pit depth, overhead clearance, and machine-room ventilation per manufacturer and ASME A17.1. Start submittals at contract award; no hoistway work is complete until inspector witness test and state certificate.

title: CSI Division 31 Earthwork
content: Mass grading, cut/fill balance, and export/import tracking affect cost and schedule. Verify geotechnical report recommendations for over-excavation and structural fill; proof-roll subgrade before placing aggregate base or vapor barrier.

title: CSI Division 32 Exterior Improvements
content: Paving, curbs, sidewalks, and landscaping close out the site. Asphalt placement needs compacted subgrade and minimum ambient/base temperatures; concrete flatwork requires control joints and curing before traffic. Coordinate irrigation blow-out for cold climates.

title: CSI Division 33 Utilities
content: Site utilities (water, sewer, storm, gas, electric) require utility locates (811), trench safety, and pressure testing before backfill. As-built survey and record drawings are required for easements and future maintenance access.

title: BIM and VDC Coordination
content: Building Information Modeling clash detection (Navisworks/Solibri) should run at 30%, 60%, and 90% design milestones and again at fabrication-level LOD 350. Federated models need agreed origin, shared coordinates, and a single clash matrix owner assigned to each trade.

title: Drone Survey and Progress Monitoring
content: UAV photogrammetry supports stockpile volume calculations, earthwork progress verification, and as-built roof surveys. FAA Part 107 certification, NOTAM/TFR checks, and site-specific flight plans are required before operating on active job sites.

title: Lean Construction and Last Planner System
content: Last Planner System uses weekly work planning with constraint analysis, PPC (percent plan complete) tracking, and lookahead schedules to reduce variability. Daily huddles surface blockers before they hit the critical path.

title: Modular Off-Site Construction Logistics
content: Volumetric modular delivery requires crane pick plans, route surveys for oversize transport, and weather windows for set-day lifts. Module weatherproofing caps and temporary bracing must stay in place until permanent connections are inspected.

title: Thermal Imaging and Building Envelope Commissioning
content: Infrared thermography during blower-door testing reveals air leakage paths and missing insulation. ASTM E1186 and RESNET standards guide acceptable temperature differentials; remediate before close-in when possible to avoid destructive rework.

title: Construction Daily Report Best Practices
content: Daily reports should capture weather (for delay documentation), manpower by trade, equipment on site, work performed, deliveries, visitors, safety incidents/near-misses, and RFI/submittal status. Photos with date/time/GPS strengthen delay and extra-work claims.

title: Prevailing Wage and Certified Payroll
content: Public works projects require Davis-Bacon or state prevailing wage rates by classification, with certified payroll (WH-347) submitted weekly. Misclassification of laborers vs. operators is a common audit finding — job descriptions must match actual tasks performed.
